verdict.rationale: Brex documents a broad public API surface covering most of what the UI does: accounting, budgets, team/users/cards, expenses with receipt uploads, payments via ACH, wires and checks, transactions and statements, onboarding, travel, and webhooks, plus an official MCP server. However, nothing documents UI parity, and some UI capabilities appear only partly exposed: the Travel API is view-only while the UI supports in-app bookings and itinerary changes, and AI invoice entry and one-click accrual booking have no documented API equivalents. Missing for 10: an explicit API/UI parity commitment, write access for travel bookings, API coverage for invoice automation and accruals, and independent hands-on confirmation of coverage.
